binary-search.title: Shrink the remaining sorted range
binary-search.summary: Arrows show the inclusive-range algorithm. Sorted input under the same comparison is a precondition; a matching index need not be the first duplicate.

nodes.label: Remaining low..high
nodes.description: Start with 0 through len(values)-1.

nodes.label: Range nonempty?
nodes.description: Continue only while low <= high.

nodes.label: Compare middle
nodes.description: Compute mid and compare values[mid] with target.

nodes.label: Found index
nodes.description: Equality returns mid.

nodes.label: Shrink range
nodes.description: Below target: low=mid+1. Above target: high=mid-1.

nodes.label: Missing: -1
nodes.description: An empty range means no matching value was found.

steps.title: Check the invariant
steps.explanation: If an unfound target exists it stays in the remaining range. Empty input immediately returns -1.

steps.title: Match or exclude
steps.explanation: Return on equality; otherwise discard the middle and the side that cannot contain the target.

steps.title: Repeat on a smaller range
steps.explanation: Every update shrinks the interval, eventually finding a match or exhausting it.

topological.title: Dependencies and ready vertices
topological.summary: A dependency edge means its source must precede its target. Kahn's algorithm removes dependencies and rejects a cycle when not all vertices are emitted.

nodes.label: Count incoming edges
nodes.description: Include neighbor-only vertices in the vertex set.

nodes.label: Ready queue
nodes.description: Queue vertices with zero remaining prerequisites.

nodes.label: Emit next vertex
nodes.description: Remove a ready vertex and append it to the order.

nodes.label: Remove outgoing dependencies
nodes.description: Decrement each neighbor indegree; enqueue neighbors that reach zero.

nodes.label: Check emitted count
nodes.description: When the queue empties, compare order length with vertex count.

nodes.label: Valid order
nodes.description: Equal counts mean every vertex was emitted.

nodes.label: Cycle error
nodes.description: Unequal counts raise dependency cycle.

steps.title: Find initially ready vertices
steps.explanation: Vertices with no incoming dependencies can come first.

steps.title: Remove one dependency layer
steps.explanation: Emit a ready vertex and update neighbors. Multiple valid orders may exist.

steps.title: Check completeness
steps.explanation: A partial order is not success: un-emitted vertices reveal a directed cycle.

dijkstra.title: A cheaper detour beats the direct edge
dijkstra.summary: The lesson graph has A to B cost 8, A to C cost 2 and C to B cost 1. Nonnegative weights support this distance reasoning.

nodes.label: A: cost 0
nodes.description: The start has distance zero.

nodes.label: C: cost 2
nodes.description: The first relaxation discovers C at cost 2.

nodes.label: B candidate: 8
nodes.description: The direct edge initially proposes B at cost 8.

nodes.label: B improved: 3
nodes.description: Popping C proposes 2+1=3, replacing the best-known distance to B.

nodes.label: Old B=8 entry skipped
nodes.description: The old heap entry remains but is stale once B has distance 3.

steps.title: Discover candidates
steps.explanation: After exploring A, the heap contains C at 2 and B at 8.

steps.title: Relax through the cheapest candidate
steps.explanation: Pop C first and improve B to 3. First discovery is not finalization.

steps.title: Skip obsolete work
steps.explanation: When the old B=8 entry is popped, it differs from distance[B] and is skipped.

two-pointers.title: Move the pointer that can improve the sum
two-pointers.summary: Sorted input makes the discard argument valid. The two indexes refer to the sorted input.

nodes.label: Opposite endpoints
nodes.description: Initialize left=0 and right=len(values)-1.

nodes.label: left < right?
nodes.description: Require two distinct positions.

nodes.label: Compare sum
nodes.description: Compare values[left]+values[right] with the target.

nodes.label: Return pair
nodes.description: Equal sum returns the two indexes.

nodes.label: Move one endpoint
nodes.description: Too small: left+=1. Too large: right-=1.

nodes.label: No pair
nodes.description: If endpoints meet, return None.

steps.title: Require two positions
steps.explanation: Empty and one-value inputs have no two distinct positions.

steps.title: Use ordering to discard
steps.explanation: A too-small sum needs a larger left value; a too-large sum needs a smaller right value.

steps.title: Terminate as the interval shrinks
steps.explanation: Each move shortens the interval; the loop ends with a pair or None.

backtracking.title: Choose, recurse, restore
backtracking.summary: The subset generator explores exclusion first, then inclusion. A copied result preserves each leaf independently.

nodes.label: visit(index)
nodes.description: The state is index plus selected values.

nodes.label: At end?
nodes.description: Compare index with the number of inputs.

nodes.label: Copy selected
nodes.description: At a leaf append selected.copy() and return.

nodes.label: Exclude current item
nodes.description: Visit index+1 without appending the item.

nodes.label: Include current item
nodes.description: Append the current item, then visit index+1.

nodes.label: Restore selected
nodes.description: Pop the appended item when the include branch returns.

steps.title: Recognize a finished subset
steps.explanation: At the final index copy the selection, so later edits cannot change that output.

steps.title: Explore both choices
steps.explanation: The exclusion branch completes before appending and exploring inclusion.

steps.title: Restore the parent state
steps.explanation: Pop after inclusion so the caller sees the selection it had before this choice.

knapsack.title: Read previous-item states by moving downward
knapsack.summary: For one item of weight 2/value 3 at capacity 4, descending capacity prevents using that item twice. The correct 0/1 value is 3.

nodes.label: Previous dp: all zero
nodes.description: Before the only item, every capacity allows the empty selection.

nodes.label: Capacity 4
nodes.description: Read previous dp[2]=0 and set dp[4]=max(0,0+3)=3.

nodes.label: Capacity 3
nodes.description: Read previous dp[1]=0 and set dp[3]=3.

nodes.label: Capacity 2
nodes.description: Read previous dp[0]=0 and set dp[2]=3.

nodes.label: Answer dp[4]=3
nodes.description: The capacity-4 cell was computed before dp[2] changed.

steps.title: Start from the previous item prefix
steps.explanation: Every source state is zero before processing this one item.

steps.title: Move downward
steps.explanation: Capacities 4, 3, 2 read lower cells before those cells are updated this pass.

steps.title: Take the item once
steps.explanation: dp[4] stays 3. An upward traversal would reuse newly updated dp[2] and incorrectly produce 6.

algorithm-review.title: Three kinds of algorithm evidence
algorithm-review.summary: The lesson review checklist asks for a correctness argument, a cost argument and tests. The diagram organizes evidence; benchmarks alone prove neither correctness nor asymptotic growth.

nodes.label: Contract and invariant
nodes.description: Define valid inputs, promised results and the property maintained during work.

nodes.label: Termination and result
nodes.description: Show progress toward termination and why the final result meets the contract.

nodes.label: Representation and cost
nodes.description: Name the representation, counted operations and worst-case bound.

nodes.label: Independent checks
nodes.description: Compare a bounded simple oracle and adversarial cases; state resource limits.
